1.

Heard Shri Prem Sagar Verma, learned counsel for the petitioner, Shri Gopal Chandra Saxena,
learned Standing Counsel for the State-respondents and perused the material brought on the record.

2. The present writ petition has been filed seeking the issuance of an appropriate writ, order, or direction in the nature of mandamus, directing the concerned respondent authorities not to dispossess the petitioner from her Abadi land Gata No.310 and 311 (Old No. 176 and 178) having area of 0.025 hectare, situated in Village Kotiya, Tehsil Chail, District Kaushambi.
The petitioner has further prayed for a direction to respondent no.2 to consider and decide representation dated 21.02.2025, in accordance with law and within a stipulated time.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner is the recorded Bhumidhar with transferable rights in respect of Gata Nos. 310 and 311, ad-measuring a total area of 250 square meters, which stands duly recorded in the revenue records.
The said land has also been declared as Abadi land belonging to the petitioner.

Learned counsel further submitted that for the purpose of widening the road, the respondent authorities have undertaken a project for construction of a four-lane road, wherein the petitioner's land forms part of the proposed alignment.
In pursuance of the said project, the respondents have made partial disbursement of compensation, limited only to the structure (residential house) existing upon the said land.
However, no compensation whatsoever has been paid to the petitioner in respect of the land itself.

It is contended that the respondents,
without initiating or complying with the mandatory and statutory procedure prescribed under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act of 2013'), and without issuance of any notification, have proceeded to encroach upon and utilize the petitioner's land for the construction of the four-lane road, thereby depriving the petitioner of his property without payment of lawful compensation and in violation of Article 300-A of the Constitution of India.
4.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: On the other hand, learned Standing Counsel submits that the matter may be referred to the Committee for determining compensation, if any, in terms of Government Order dated 12.05.2016.
5. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, this Court is of the view that no useful purpose would be served in keeping the writ petition pending.

Accordingly, with the consent of the parties, the writ petition is disposed of with liberty to the petitioners to submit a fresh representation before the District Level Committee, detailing all their grievances.

In the event such a representation is submitted within two weeks from today, the District Level Committee shall consider and decide the same on its own merits and in accordance with law, after affording an opportunity of hearing to all stakeholders.
The decision shall be taken expeditiously, preferably within a period of two months from the date of submission of the representation, keeping in view the Government Order dated 12.05.2016.
